source.title: Semantic Space Search Trajectory Networks
source.authors: Julian Agudelo; A. Tonda; Gabriela Ochoa; Vincent Guigue; Cristina E. Manfredotti; Evelyne Lutton

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains MLPs on true and shuffled labels and reports training and test performance, but uses these experiments to compare semantic-space trajectory networks rather than to reproduce the original studies’ full analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior claims about modest extra training time and regularization in its background; those are not this study's results. Its own label-corruption experiment reports graph metrics in Figure 6, not training or test performance at each corruption level.
record.test_reason: The study repeats the true-versus-randomized-label experiment using fixed MLP architectures and SGD hyperparameters and reports training and test accuracy. Its additional STN analysis does not change the direct test of V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the main conclusion: real-label training produces denser, more efficient, and more centralized STNs than shuffled-label training. Table 5 supports near-perfect classification training fit with shuffled labels and degraded test performance. The broader statement that all networks successfully fit both regimes should retain the reported regression qualification: shuffled-label training R² is 0.960 for cars and 0.949 for cpu activity.
record.recipe_differences: The study follows the true-versus-shuffled-label comparison attributed to Zhang et al., using its own MLP configurations and fixed optimization hyperparameters across label conditions; it does not report the original study's full set of experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The MNIST corruption experiment varies label corruption fraction, but reports graph metrics rather than fit or test error at those levels.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST STN efficiency, maximum closeness, and maximum PageRank decline monotonically with increasing uniform label corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing label corruption produces less efficient and less centralized semantic-space trajectory graphs.

record.problems: The randomization results are reported as means and standard deviations over 20 runs on one fold; only MLP configurations are evaluated in this experiment. Partial-corruption graph metrics do not establish training fit or test error at those levels.

untested.parts: Architecture and optimizer breadth beyond the tested fixed MLP configuration.
Relative time to fit true and random labels and convergence speed across corruption levels; equal training budgets do not establish equal convergence times.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across partial corruption levels; Figure 6 reports graph metrics only.
Effects of applying or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise; trajectory topology does not establish this temporal order.

missing.what: Bioresponse classification training and test accuracy: real labels 1.000 ± 0.000 and 0.793 ± 0.009; shuffled labels 0.999 ± 0.000 and 0.478 ± 0.013. Same MLPcls protocol, 20 runs.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Background statements about modest extra training time and explicit regularization are cited results, not additional tests. Regression R² results do not directly establish V1's classification-error and chance-performance formulation.

versions.untested_parts: The reported MLP experiments cover the listed classification datasets, not a range of standard architectures or optimizer settings; the study does not test unstructured inputs.
The study does not report training time or convergence speed across label corruption levels.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment is reported.
At partial corruption levels, the study reports graph metrics, not training fit or test error.
The study does not test weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal.
The study does not measure learning order or compare patterns learned over training.
